KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.hero.title: Glass Skin Method
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.hero.sub: Glass skin is luminous, ultra-hydrated, see-through-clear skin. It isn't a product — it's a layering technique. Here's the exact protocol: how to hydrate on damp skin, how many toner layers (the named 7-skin method) for YOUR skin type, the ingredient stack, and realistic timelines.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.hero.disclaimer: Glass skin describes a cosmetic, hydrated finish — not a medical outcome. Results vary; these steps support skin's look and feel, they do not treat skin conditions.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.0.title: Hydrate on damp skin
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.0.body: Humectants (HA, glycerin, betaglucan) pull water from whatever's nearest. On damp skin they pull moisture IN; on bone-dry skin in low humidity they can pull it OUT. Apply each watery layer while the last is still slightly tacky.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.1.title: Many thin layers, not one thick one
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.1.body: The glass-skin signature is depth of hydration, built by layering several lightweight watery products rather than one heavy cream. Thin layers absorb; thick layers pill and sit on top.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.2.title: Thinnest → thickest
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.2.body: Move from the most watery (toner) to the most emollient (cream, then SPF or sleeping mask). Water can't penetrate an oil layer applied first.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.3.title: Always seal the water in
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.3.body: Humectant layers without an occlusive/emollient seal can evaporate and leave skin tight. The final cream (AM) or sleeping mask (PM) locks the hydration in — this is the step most people skip.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.4.title: Press, don't rub
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.4.body: Pat each layer in with warm palms or press with fingertips. Rubbing causes pilling and disrupts the layer underneath.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.5.title: Glass skin lives and dies by SPF
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.principles.5.body: All the hydration in the world looks dull under UV damage, and brightening progress reverses without it. Daily SPF 50+ PA++++ is non-negotiable for the clear, even tone half of the look.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.title: The 7-Skin Method (7스킨법)
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.what: A Korean technique where you layer a hydrating toner ("skin" is the Korean word for toner) multiple times — pressing each layer in before the next — to flood skin with lightweight hydration. "7" is the famous number, not a rule: you tune the count to your skin and the weather.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.how: Use a hydrating, alcohol-free toner (look for HA, glycerin, betaglucan, panthenol — not an exfoliating/astringent toner). Dispense into palms or a cotton pad, press over the face, wait ~20–30 seconds until tacky, repeat. Stop while skin still feels comfortable, never sticky or overloaded.
Dry and dehydrated skin benefits most from the full method. Layer generously, then seal hard with a ceramide cream. In winter, slug on top.
A comfortable middle ground for plump, dewy skin without heaviness.
Go heavier on dry cheeks, lighter on the oily T-zone. You can layer fewer times in the T-zone.
Use a watery, oil-free toner and fewer layers — over-layering can feel greasy and congest. Hydration still matters: dehydrated oily skin overproduces oil.
Fewer layers of a fragrance-free, minimal-ingredient toner (betaglucan/panthenol/centella). Patch test first; build up slowly.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.mistakes.0: Using an exfoliating or alcohol toner instead of a pure hydrating one — the #1 way to wreck your barrier chasing glass skin.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.mistakes.1: Layering on dry skin in a dry room — seal each round before it fully evaporates.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.mistakes.2: Skipping the final cream/occlusive — water layers alone evaporate and leave skin tighter than before.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.sevenSkin.mistakes.3: Adding 7 layers when your skin only wants 3 — stickiness, pilling and clogged pores follow. More layers ≠ more glass.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.title: The glass-skin protocol
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.intro: An AM and a PM sequence. The AM build is about a dewy, protected daytime glow; the PM build is about deep overnight repair. Tune the 7-skin layer count to your skin type above.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.0.why: Start with a clean, slightly damp face — don't strip. Leave skin barely towel-patted, not bone dry.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.1.why: The hydration base. Press in your skin-type's layer count of a watery, alcohol-free toner.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.2.why: A ferment/rice/snail essence on still-damp skin adds the luminous, bouncy depth that reads as 'glass'.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.3.why: Vitamin C + niacinamide even tone and add antioxidant defense — the 'clear & even' half of glass skin. (Use vitamin C in the AM.)
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.4.why: Seal all that water in with a non-heavy cream so it doesn't evaporate. Don't skip this.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.am.5.why: Glass skin is impossible to maintain without it — UV dulls tone and undoes brightening. Reapply midday.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.0.why: Oil cleanser to melt SPF/makeup, then a gentle water cleanser. A truly clean canvas is what lets layers absorb.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.1.why: Rebuild the hydration base at night, when skin repairs and absorbs most.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.2.why: Press a ferment/snail/propolis layer into damp skin for overnight glow and bounce.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.3.why: On repair nights, a PDRN/peptide ampoule for bounce; on separate nights, a slow-introduced retinol for long-term clarity & texture (PM only, then SPF next day).
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.4.why: A richer ceramide cream at night locks everything in and rebuilds the barrier that holds water.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.protocol.pm.5.why: For very dry skin or winter, a thin occlusive sleeping-mask layer maximizes overnight hydration — wake up to plump, glassy skin.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.ingredientStack.title: The glass-skin ingredient stack
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.ingredientStack.intro: These cross-reference the Ingredient Encyclopedia — tap any to learn more. The look is built on hydrators + brighteners + barrier-sealers.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.title: Realistic timelines — what to actually expect
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.intro: Glass skin builds in stages. Hydration shows up fast; tone and clarity take real consistency. Anyone promising it overnight is selling, not informing.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.stages.0.body: Right after layering, skin looks dewier and feels bouncier. This is surface hydration — real, but it resets daily. Consistency is what makes it stick.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.stages.1.body: With daily layering + sealing, your skin's hydration baseline rises. Tightness fades, makeup sits better, the dewy look lasts through the day rather than disappearing by noon.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.stages.2.body: Brightening actives (vitamin C, niacinamide) + diligent SPF gradually even tone and fade marks. This is the 'see-through clarity' half of glass skin — and it only sticks with sun protection.
KBEAUTY_GLASSKIN.timeline.stages.3.body: Gentle exfoliation + retinoids/peptides over time refine the look of pores and texture, so light reflects more evenly. Slow and steady beats over-exfoliating, which sets you back.

KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.0.title: Buy from the official store or an authorized seller
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.0.desc: On marketplaces look for the brand official-store badge. First-party sites (Olive Young Global, StyleKorean) and authorized retailers (YesStyle, Stylevana) source directly from brands. Unverified third-party sellers are the number-one fake-risk for COSRX, Anua and Beauty of Joseon.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.1.title: Check the batch code and any QR or verification mark
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.1.desc: Genuine Korean products carry a printed batch/manufacture code and often a manufacture and best-before date (Korean: jejo / kkaji). Some brands add a QR or scratch-off label. A missing, smudged, stickered-over or re-printed code is a red flag.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.2.title: If the price looks too good to be true, it is
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.2.desc: Counterfeiters compete on price. A 50-80 percent off-retail listing from an unknown seller, especially on a hot item, is the most reliable fake signal. Compare against the official-store price first.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.3.title: Inspect packaging print, fonts and seals
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.3.desc: Authentic packaging has crisp printing, correct logos and an intact factory seal or shrink-wrap. Blurry text, off-color logos, spelling errors, a loose cap or a broken seal suggest a counterfeit or tampered unit.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.4.title: Judge the pump, texture, color and scent on arrival
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.4.desc: Real formulas dispense smoothly and match the described texture, color and (often subtle) scent. A sputtering pump, watery or separated texture, off smell, or wrong color versus the official photos are warning signs - stop using it.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.5.title: Beware stolen or mismatched listing photos
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.5.desc: Fakes often reuse official marketing images while shipping a different unit. Check that reviews include real customer photos and that the shipped packaging matches current official packaging (brands update designs).
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.6.title: Read recent reviews for fake complaints
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.6.desc: Scan the newest reviews and Q and A for words like fake, counterfeit, different from store, no batch code or reaction. A pattern of authenticity complaints is decisive - trust the crowd at the buy-moment.
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.7.title: Patch-test before full use
KBEAUTY_BUY.authChecklist.7.desc: Even with an authentic product, patch-test new items on your inner arm for a day or two. It protects you from genuine sensitivities and from any counterfeit slipping through - your safety net at first use.

KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.intro: Sunscreen is the single most impactful step in any routine — it helps protect against the UV exposure dermatologists link to most visible photo-ageing and uneven tone. Korea's reputation is earned: modern photostable filters (not yet FDA-approved in the US) let Korean SPF deliver high SPF/PA in feather-light, no-white-cast textures. This decoder explains the label, matches a filter type to your quiz skin type, and shows exactly how much to apply and reapply.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.0.label: SPF (Sun Protection Factor)
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.0.plain: Measures protection against UVB. SPF 50 filters ~98% of UVB in lab testing; SPF 50+ means it tested beyond 50. The jump from SPF 30 to 50 is small in theory but meaningful in the real world, where almost no one applies the full lab amount.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.1.label: PA (Protection Grade of UVA)
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.1.measures: UVA — the deeper ageing & pigment rays
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.1.plain: The Asian (PPD-based) measure of UVA protection — the rays tied to long-term ageing, sagging and dark spots, which pass through glass and cloud. More plus signs = more UVA defence: PA+ (some), PA++ (moderate), PA+++ (high), PA++++ (highest). Western labels show this as 'Broad Spectrum' instead.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.2.label: Broad Spectrum
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.2.plain: The Western (US/EU) wording confirming a sunscreen guards against both UVB and UVA. A Korean PA++++ SPF50+ is the equivalent of a high broad-spectrum rating — same goal, different label system.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.3.label: PPD (Persistent Pigment Darkening)
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.3.measures: The raw UVA number behind PA
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.3.plain: The underlying UVA score the PA grade is built on. PA++++ corresponds to a PPD of 16 or higher. You'll mostly see PA on the front; PPD sometimes appears on the back of premium Korean labels.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.4.label: Water / Sweat Resistant
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.decodeTable.4.plain: Means the SPF holds up for a stated time (e.g. 40 or 80 minutes) of swimming or sweating before you must reapply — not that it's waterproof. Great for beach, sport and humid Korean summers.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.how: Carbon-based filters absorb UV and convert it to a tiny amount of heat. This is where Korea shines — newer filters such as Tinosorb S/M, Uvinul A Plus and Uvinul T 150 (common in EU/Korea, not yet US-approved) give very high protection in elegant, invisible textures.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.pros.1: No white cast — invisible on every skin tone
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.pros.3: Often the most cosmetically elegant SPF you can buy
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.cons.0: Needs ~15–20 min to set before sun (apply as last AM step)
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.cons.1: A few filters can sting very reactive eyes/skin
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.0.skinNote: The default pick for most skin — especially oily and combination, where light gel-creams beat heavy mineral layers.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.how: Zinc oxide and/or titanium dioxide form a protective layer on the skin's surface that mostly reflects and scatters UV (and partly absorbs it). Inherently gentle and photostable, so they're the classic choice for reactive skin and post-procedure days.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.pros.0: Very gentle — friendly for sensitive & reactive skin
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.pros.1: Works the moment it's applied (no wait)
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.pros.2: Photostable; a good post-peel / post-laser option
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.cons.0: Can leave a white or grey cast — most visible on deep skin tones
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.cons.2: Needs careful, even rubbing to avoid patchiness
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.finish: Matte to natural; may show a slight cast
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.1.skinNote: Best for sensitive, reactive or post-treatment skin. On medium-to-deep tones, look for tinted mineral formulas to cancel the cast.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.2.how: Blends a little mineral filter with chemical filters to get the best of both: gentle, photostable protection with a lighter, less-casty finish than a pure mineral SPF.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.2.cons.0: Can still leave a faint cast
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.2.cons.1: Finish varies a lot by formula
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.filterTypes.2.skinNote: A smart middle path if mineral feels too heavy but pure chemical feels too active for you.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.headline: The amount is everything — and so is reapplying
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.0.title: The two-finger rule
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.0.text: Squeeze sunscreen along your index and middle fingers, tip to base — that's roughly the right amount for face and neck. Most people use a third of this and lose most of the rated protection.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.1.title: About ¼ teaspoon for the face
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.1.text: Another way to picture it: roughly 1.25 ml (a quarter teaspoon) for the face alone, plus more for ears, neck and any exposed skin. Under-applying turns SPF 50 into something far lower.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.2.title: Last AM step, then makeup
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.rules.2.text: Apply as the final skincare step on top of moisturizer, before makeup. Let a chemical SPF set for ~15 minutes before sun exposure.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.methods.0.text: Swipe-and-go reapplication that glides over makeup with zero mess — ideal for the midday top-up on cheeks, nose and hairline. Press, don't drag, for an even layer.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.methods.1.text: An SPF-infused cushion compact pats protection back on over makeup while refreshing your finish — the most makeup-friendly way to reapply.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.methods.2.text: Mists and brush-on SPF powders are handy for hair partings, body and quick touch-ups, but go heavy and even — it's easy to under-apply with these formats.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.reapply.cadence: For long days outdoors, reapply roughly every two hours, and after heavy sweating, swimming or towelling. For a normal indoor day, a solid morning application plus one midday top-up goes a long way.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.headline: Korean vs Western sunscreen — why the texture gap?
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.points.0: Korea and the EU can use modern UV filters (Tinosorb, Uvinul, etc.) that the US FDA hasn't approved for general use. These give high, stable protection in much lighter textures.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.points.1: Korean SPF is formulated like skincare — watery essences, fresh gels and serum-like fluids — so daily SPF actually feels good to wear and re-wear.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.points.2: Most Korean daily sunscreens are chemical or low-cast hybrids, so they disappear on the skin. For deeper tones, choose chemical or tinted formulas and skip high-zinc mineral sticks for the face.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.points.3: No-cast chemical formulas and tinted SPFs are the friendliest for medium-to-deep skin. Patch-test on the jaw first to confirm zero residue before committing to all-over use.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.koreanVsWestern.points.4: A Korean 'SPF50+ PA++++' is broadly equivalent to a Western 'Broad Spectrum SPF 50' — both target high UVB + UVA defence. The numbers are read differently, but the goal is the same.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.0.highlights.0: Rice + grain extracts for a comfortable, dewy finish
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.0.highlights.2: Doubles as a glowy makeup base
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.0.blurb: The internet's gateway Korean sunscreen — a lightweight chemical SPF with a dewy, skincare-like feel and no white cast.

KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.1.highlights.2: Gentle enough for daily reactive-skin wear
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.1.blurb: A hydrating daily chemical sunscreen built around birch sap — comfortable for dry and easily-dehydrated skin.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.2.highlights.0: Centella (cica) to help comfort the skin
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.2.highlights.1: Airy, lightweight feel that layers cleanly

KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.3.blurb: A fragrance-free, vegan chemical sunscreen aimed at sensitive skin that still wants an elegant, no-cast finish.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.4.highlights.0: Hyaluronic acid for a watery, hydrating gel feel
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.4.highlights.1: Gentle mineral-based protection for reactive skin
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.4.blurb: For sensitive skin that prefers mineral filters — a watery, hyaluronic gel-type SPF that's far less heavy than classic mineral creams.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.5.highlights.0: Twist-up stick for mess-free reapply over makeup
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.5.highlights.1: Hybrid filters for a low-cast finish

KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.picks.6.blurb: A long-running value favourite — a milky essence-type chemical SPF that absorbs fast with no cast, great for oily and combination skin.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.0.q: Do I need SPF indoors / on cloudy days?
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.0.a: UVA passes through cloud and glass, so daily SPF still helps even indoors near windows or on grey days. Heavy daily exposure is mostly incidental.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.1.q: Is a higher SPF always better?
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.1.a: Going from SPF 30 to 50 adds modest lab protection, but real-world generous, even application and reapplication matter far more than chasing the biggest number.
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.2.q: Can my makeup or moisturizer SPF replace sunscreen?
KBEAUTY_SUNCARE.myth.2.a: Usually not — people rarely apply makeup thickly or evenly enough to hit the rated SPF. Treat any SPF in makeup as a bonus on top of a dedicated sunscreen.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.title: Snail Mucin: Is the Hype Real?
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.tagline: The 'weird but it works' gateway product that turned the world on to K-beauty — explained honestly, then matched to your shelf.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.what.headline: What it actually is
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.what.body: Snail secretion filtrate (SSF) is the filtered, purified mucin a snail naturally produces. Modern Korean labs harvest it without harming the animal, then filter and standardise it. It is a complex blend of humectants and skin-loving molecules — naturally occurring hyaluronic acid, glycoproteins, glycolic acid, zinc and antioxidants — which is why a single ingredient can hydrate, smooth and add slip all at once.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.what.molecules.0.role: Draws water into the skin for that plump, dewy look
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.what.molecules.1.role: Add the signature cushiony 'slip' and a smoother surface feel
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.what.molecules.3.role: A gentle smoothing touch — far milder than a dedicated AHA
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.headline: The honest hype-check
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.real.0: It is a genuinely excellent, lightweight hydrator — the dewy, bouncy 'glass-skin' finish people post about is real and immediate.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.real.1: It layers under almost anything and rarely causes problems, which is why it became the beginner's gateway product.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.real.2: Many people love how it makes post-blemish marks and rough texture look smoother over weeks of consistent use.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.hype.0: It is a cosmetic hydrator that supports the look and feel of skin — not a medicine. It does not heal wounds or treat acne, scars or ageing.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.hype.1: Human clinical evidence is still limited and mostly small studies; most of the love is cosmetic and anecdotal (which is fine — that is what skincare is).
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.hype.2: Results are gradual and depend on consistency. A 96% essence is mostly mucin; a '10,000ppm' cream is a marketing number, not a guaranteed strength.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.hypeCheck.bottomLine: Verdict: worth the hype as a do-it-all hydrator that feels lovely and plays well with everything — just buy it for glow and comfort, not as a cure.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.headline: How to layer it (the part most people get wrong)
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.0.title: Apply to damp skin
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.0.text: Pat it on right after toner or essence while skin is still slightly damp — humectants like snail mucin pull in nearby water, so damp skin gives a bigger plumping payoff.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.1.title: Press, don't rub
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.1.text: Pat and press a thin layer until it turns tacky. It is naturally stringy — that 'slip' is normal and means it's working, not that you used too much.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.2.title: Seal it in with moisturiser
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.2.text: Always follow with a cream or lotion. A humectant left bare in dry air can pull water out of skin — the cream locks the moisture in.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.3.title: AM or PM (or both)
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.howToUse.steps.3.text: Gentle enough for twice daily. In the AM it sits happily under sunscreen; in the PM it's a soothing buffer after stronger actives.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.headline: Who it suits
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.great.0.why: A featherlight way to flood skin with water before sealing with cream.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.great.1.why: The instant dewy slip is the fast lane to that lit-from-within look.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.great.2.why: Hydrating without heaviness — comfortable even on an oily T-zone.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.great.3.why: Usually fragrance-free and very low-irritation; a gentle barrier-friendly hydrator.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.watchOuts.0.wh: Loved for marks and hydration, but some find richer snail creams a little tacky — choose a light essence over a heavy cream.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.suitability.watchOuts.1.wh: Patch-test and avoid if you react to mollusc/shellfish-type ingredients.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.pairs.headline: Pairs beautifully with
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.pairs.note: It is a peacemaker — it has no known conflicts and even helps buffer the sting of stronger actives like retinol or exfoliating acids.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.headline: COSRX Snail 96 vs the alternatives
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.subhead: The original hero next to four worthy picks — so you can grab the icon or a cheaper dupe.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.tableNote: Picks reflect each product's widely published positioning. Prices vary by region and seller; tap a card to see today's live AliExpress listings.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.picks.0.vibe: The global phenomenon people search by name. A near-pure, no-frills mucin essence — the safe first buy and the benchmark everything else is measured against.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.picks.1.vibe: Pairs snail mucin with calming centella for blemish-prone, marked or reactive skin. The pick if you want soothing plus hydration in one step.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.picks.2.vibe: A trend-forward house that blends mucin with brightening niacinamide. Great for anyone chasing tone and glow alongside hydration.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.picks.3.vibe: One of the OG snail lines, beloved for value. The richer ampoule and cream suit drier skin or anyone who wants more cushion than an essence.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.compare.picks.4.vibe: A cult, gently-formulated essence for sensitive, troubled skin. Note the bee-derived ingredient — skip if you have a bee-product sensitivity.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.0.q: Is snail mucin cruelty-free? Are snails harmed?
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.0.a: Reputable Korean producers collect the secretion in low-stress conditions without killing the snail. It is, however, an animal-derived ingredient, so it is not vegan or vegetarian.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.1.a: Snail mucin itself is low on the comedogenic scale and is a favourite of acne-prone users for hydration and the look of post-blemish marks. If you break out, a richer snail cream's other ingredients are the more likely cause — try a lighter essence.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.2.q: Essence, serum or cream — which do I buy?
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.2.a: Start with a high-percentage essence (like a 96%) for the purest, most universal experience. Choose a cream only if your skin is dry and wants more cushion, or a centella/niacinamide blend if you're targeting marks or glow.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.3.q: Can I use it with retinol or vitamin C?
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.faq.3.a: Yes — it has no known conflicts and actually helps buffer the irritation from stronger actives. Apply the active first, then snail mucin as a soothing hydration layer, then your cream.
KBEAUTY_SNAIL.disclaimer: Educational information about cosmetic ingredients, not medical advice. Cosmetics support the look and feel of skin; they do not treat or cure any condition. Patch-test new products and see a dermatologist for persistent concerns.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.intro: Korean product names don't map 1:1 to Western shelves, which is why "do I really need a toner AND an essence AND a serum?" is the #1 beginner question. The honest answer: textures sit on a thin-to-thick scale, you layer lightest first, and most people only need 3-4 of these. Slide through them below to see what each one actually does — and which you can skip.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.0.job: Step 1 of the double cleanse — dissolves oil-based grime (sunscreen, makeup, sebum) that water alone can't lift.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.0.needWhy: Non-negotiable at night if you wear sunscreen or makeup — water cleansers can't break down water-resistant SPF.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.0.skipIf: AM only, or nights with bare, SPF-free skin (then a single water cleanse is plenty).
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.0.tip: Massage onto DRY hands and DRY face for 30-60s, then add a splash of water to emulsify (it turns milky) before rinsing.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.1.job: Step 2 of the double cleanse — lifts away sweat, dirt and any leftover residue without stripping the barrier.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.1.needWhy: The one cleanser everyone needs, morning and night. Low-pH (around 5.5) keeps the barrier calm.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.1.skipIf: Never fully skip — but in the morning a quick water rinse can replace it for very dry skin.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.1.tip: Lukewarm water only. Hot water and squeaky-clean tightness are signs you're over-stripping.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.2.job: First hydration + prep step. Korean toners rebalance and soften skin so the next layers absorb better. They hydrate — they do not strip.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.2.needWhy: A genuinely useful prep + hydration layer, and the base of the "7-skin" method. Skin-friendly even for beginners.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.2.skipIf: You're keeping it ultra-minimal — a hydrating essence or moisturizer can cover the same hydration job.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.2.tip: Forget Western alcohol astringents. A K-beauty toner should feel like watery hydration; pat 1-3 layers into damp skin.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.3.job: The signature "heart" of a K-beauty routine: a lightweight hydration + glow layer that sits between toner and serum.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.3.needWhy: Lovely for glow and that dewy finish, but it overlaps with a hydrating toner. Plenty of great routines skip it.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.3.skipIf: You already use a hydrating toner and a serum — the essence is the most skippable of the three.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.3.tip: "First essence" / ferment essences (galactomyces, rice) are the radiance ones; press into damp skin with palms.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.4.job: Your targeted treatment — a concentrated dose of one or two actives for a specific concern (brightening, calming, firming).
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.4.needWhy: If you have a concern you actually want to address, this is the step that does the work. Choose by goal, not by hype.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.4.skipIf: You have no specific concern and just want healthy, hydrated maintenance skin.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.4.tip: AM = antioxidants like vitamin C under SPF. PM = retinol or exfoliating actives. One hero serum is usually enough.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.5.job: Essentially a more concentrated serum — a higher dose of an active for a focused, often short-term boost.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.5.needWhy: "Ampoule" vs "serum" is mostly a marketing/strength distinction, not a separate routine step. Pick one for the treatment slot.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.5.skipIf: You already use a serum — you don't need both an ampoule and a serum every day.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.5.tip: Treat it as your strongest treatment. If a serum feels too gentle for a stubborn concern, an ampoule is the step up.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.6.job: A lightweight milky moisturizer that seals in hydration without the weight of a cream.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.6.needWhy: It's simply a lighter alternative to cream. Useful for oily/combination skin or hot, humid weather — not an extra step.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.6.skipIf: You use a cream — an emulsion and a cream do the same sealing job. Pick the texture your skin likes.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.6.tip: Oily or combination skin in summer often prefers an emulsion; dry skin in winter usually wants a cream.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.7.job: The seal. Ceramides and humectants lock everything underneath in and reinforce the barrier — the last skincare step before SPF.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.7.needWhy: Everyone needs something to seal in moisture. Whether it's a gel-cream or a rich balm depends on your skin and season.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.7.skipIf: Never fully skip the seal — but very oily skin can use a light gel-cream or an emulsion instead of a heavy cream.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.items.7.tip: This is where the thinnest-to-thickest rule ends. Layer humectants underneath on damp skin, then seal with cream.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.minimalRoutine.title: The honest minimum
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.minimalRoutine.body: You don't need all of these. A complete routine can be just four steps: cleanse → hydrate (toner or essence) → treat (one serum) → seal (moisturizer), plus SPF in the morning. Add an essence, ampoule or emulsion only if you enjoy them or have a reason to.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.title: Double cleansing, explained
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.subtitl: Two cleansers, one at night — the foundation of clear K-beauty skin.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.what: Double cleansing means washing your face twice at night: first an oil-based cleanser, then a water-based one. It is a PM-only ritual — you do not need to double cleanse in the morning.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.steps.0: Massage an oil cleanser or balm onto dry hands and a dry face for 30-60 seconds. Oil dissolves oil — it melts sunscreen, makeup and the day's sebum that water can't touch. Add a little water to emulsify (it goes milky), then rinse.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.steps.1: Follow with a gentle low-pH water cleanser (gel or foam) to wash away the emulsified oil, sweat and dirt — leaving skin clean but never tight or stripped.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.why: Most modern sunscreens and long-wear makeup are oil- and water-resistant by design — a single water cleanser smears them around instead of removing them. The oil step lifts that layer off so the water step can finish the job. Properly removing SPF and grime at night is one of the most-cited habits for clearer, calmer skin.
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.dos.0: Oil cleanser on DRY skin, then emulsify with water
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.dos.2: PM only — single cleanse is fine in the AM
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.donts.0: Don't skip the water cleanse after the oil
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.donts.1: Don't scrub or over-massage sensitive skin
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.donts.2: Don't double cleanse twice a day — it's a night ritual
KBEAUTY_CATEGORIES.doubleCleanse.ctaNote: Double cleansing needs two products: an oil cleanser/balm and a low-pH water cleanser.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.0.whatItIs: A lightweight watery toner built on a high percentage of heartleaf (Houttuynia) extract for a calming hydration layer.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.0.viralFor: The TikTok 'glass-skin in a bottle' toner — endless before/after pore-and-redness clips.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.0.evidence: Heartleaf and panthenol are well-established soothing/barrier-support ingredients, so the 'calmer, comfier skin' experience is real. The 'shrinks pores permanently' framing is the overclaim — it softens the look, it doesn't resize pores.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.0.worthIt: Yes for reactive, oily or breakout-prone skin wanting a gentle daily hydrator. Skip if you specifically need exfoliation or active treatment.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.1.whatItIs: An organic (chemical) daily sunscreen with a serum-like, no-white-cast finish.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.1.viralFor: The internet's favorite 'I actually want to reapply' SPF — a perennial Olive Young / global best-seller.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.1.evidence: Daily broad-spectrum SPF is the single best-supported anti-ageing and tone-protecting step there is. The elegant texture is the genuine differentiator; rice/probiotic extras are a pleasant bonus, not the main event.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.1.worthIt: Yes — arguably the highest-value bottle in K-beauty. The cosmetic-finish hype is, for once, deserved.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.2.whatItIs: A 'salmon-DNA' (PDRN) plus peptide range — serums, ampoules and pads marketed for a firm, bouncy 'glass-skin' look.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.2.viralFor: The face of the 2026 PDRN wave; viral 'glup-glup' bounce-test and overnight-glow clips.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.2.evidence: PDRN has clinical support as an injectable, but topical-cosmetic PDRN evidence is still emerging — expect a hydrated, plumped, glowy look rather than the same results as a clinic procedure. The supporting peptides and humectants do real cosmetic work.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.2.worthIt: A fun, well-formulated glow layer if you enjoy trying next-gen actives — just calibrate expectations to 'cosmetic plump', not 'injectable-level firming'.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.3.whatItIs: A vegan, fragrance-free multi-weight hyaluronic acid serum for fast watery hydration.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.3.viralFor: The go-to 'dewy with no stickiness' HA serum across routine-builder videos.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.3.evidence: Multiple hyaluronic-acid weights reliably draw water into the skin for a visibly plumper, smoother look. Apply on damp skin and seal — the only caveat is in very dry air HA needs an occlusive on top, which the hype clips rarely mention.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.3.worthIt: Yes — a safe, near-universal hydration workhorse, gentle enough for sensitive skin.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.4.whatItIs: A single-ingredient-forward centella (cica) ampoule for a soothing, lightweight calming layer.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.4.viralFor: The minimalist 'one-ingredient calm-down' ampoule beloved by sensitive-skin creators.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.4.evidence: Centella and its purified actives (madecassoside) are among the best-studied soothing/barrier-support botanicals in skincare, so the 'calmer, less reactive' result is well-founded.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.4.worthIt: Yes for redness-prone, stressed or post-active skin. Less essential if your barrier is already happy.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.5.whatItIs: A multi-active brightening serum blending niacinamide with tone-evening ingredients.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.5.viralFor: Viral 'glow filter IRL' tone-up clips; one of Olive Young's break-out brightening heroes.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.5.evidence: Niacinamide and tranexamic acid genuinely help even tone and fade the look of dark spots — over weeks, paired with daily SPF. The 'instant whitening' framing is the hype; real brightening is gradual, not same-day.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.5.worthIt: Yes if you want gradual tone-evening and will commit to sunscreen. No if you expect overnight results.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.6.whatItIs: A high-mucin essence famed for a glossy, plumped, dewy finish.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.6.viralFor: The original viral K-beauty hero — still a constant best-seller and 'holy grail' staple.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.6.evidence: Snail secretion filtrate is a proven cosmetic humectant/film-former — the bouncy, hydrated, glowy feel is real. 'Fades scars' is the overclaim: it supports the look of post-blemish marks, it doesn't erase true scars.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.6.worthIt: Yes as an affordable hydrating glow layer. Patch-test if you have a known mollusc sensitivity.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.7.whatItIs: A gentle deep-sea-mineral hydrating toner with very mild PHA-style exfoliation.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.7.viralFor: The 'can't-go-wrong starter toner' everyone recommends to beginners.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.7.evidence: Simple, well-tolerated hydration with a touch of gentle resurfacing — exactly what it claims, no inflated promises. Its appeal is reliability, not novelty.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.7.worthIt: Yes as a foolproof daily hydrating toner for almost any skin type.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.8.whatItIs: A long-wear cushion foundation that went viral for its unusually wide shade range.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.8.viralFor: The TikTok cushion that 'finally has my shade' — a global shade-inclusivity moment.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.8.evidence: Genuinely strong wear and a praised wide shade range — the inclusivity story is real. As a 'skincare-makeup hybrid' the skincare claims are minor; treat it as makeup with light SPF, not a treatment.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.8.worthIt: Yes as a high-coverage, long-wear cushion. Not a skincare step — keep your actives separate.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.9.whatItIs: Pre-soaked toner pads with heartleaf and calming botanicals for a quick wipe-and-soothe step.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.9.viralFor: The 'desk-drawer breakout-day rescue' pads all over routine TikTok.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.9.evidence: The soothing botanicals are well-supported, and pads add convenient mild exfoliation/refresh. The 'spot' naming oversells targeted blemish-clearing — they calm and tidy, they're not a treatment patch.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.9.worthIt: Yes for oily/reactive skin wanting a fast soothing swipe. Optional if you already use a calming toner.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.10.whatItIs: A multi-molecular-weight hyaluronic toner built for the layered '7-skin' hydration method.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.10.viralFor: The cult '7-skin method' toner for cumulative plumping.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.10.evidence: Layered humectant hydration visibly plumps and softens — the method works. Just seal with a cream so the HA pulls water in, not out, in dry climates.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.10.worthIt: Yes for dry/dehydrated skin that loves the layering ritual.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.11.whatItIs: Best-selling serum-soaked sheet masks for a fast hydration or soothing boost.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.11.viralFor: The 'buy-them-by-the-box' tourist-haul staple and pre-event glow mask.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.11.evidence: Excellent for an immediate hydration/soothing top-up before events — that part is real and instant. 'Collagen masks rebuild collagen' is the myth: topical collagen molecules don't penetrate to do that; the win is surface hydration and plump.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.11.worthIt: Yes as an occasional hydration treat. Not a daily essential or an anti-ageing 'fix'.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.12.whatItIs: A higher-strength niacinamide serum paired with tranexamic acid for tone-evening.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.12.viralFor: The 'dupe for pricey brightening serums' that blew up on review channels.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.12.evidence: Both actives are well-supported for evening tone, refining the pore look and supporting oil balance over weeks. High-percentage niacinamide can tingle on sensitive skin — start every other day.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.12.worthIt: Yes for tone, oil and pore-look concerns. Introduce slowly if you're sensitive.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.13.whatItIs: A clear hydrogel overnight mask that melts into the skin for an intense hydration seal.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.13.viralFor: The 'peel-it-off-in-the-morning glass skin' overnight mask that went mega-viral.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.13.evidence: As an occlusive hydrating overnight mask it genuinely delivers a plump, dewy morning look. The dramatic 'collagen fibres absorbing' visual is mostly the gel hydrogel doing its job — enjoy the hydration, discount the sci-fi framing.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.13.worthIt: Yes as an occasional overnight hydration boost before a big day. A treat, not a daily step.
KBEAUTY_BESTSELLERS.items.14.whatItIs: A gentle daily toner pairing mild PHA exfoliation with centella and niacinamide.

KBEAUTY_TROUBLESHOOTER_META.title: Is this working — or hurting me?
KBEAUTY_TROUBLESHOOTER_META.intro: Three quick, non-diagnostic tools to read what your skin is telling you. Educational only — these help you understand a reaction; they are not medical advice. If a reaction is severe, painful, spreading, or lasts beyond a few weeks, see a doctor or dermatologist.
KBEAUTY_TROUBLESHOOTER_META.disclaimer: Structure-function & educational information only. Not a diagnosis and not a substitute for professional medical care.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.title: Purging vs. Breakout
KBEAUTY_PURGE.subtitle: One of the most-asked K-beauty questions. Answer 4 quick questions to read your skin's reaction.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.primer: "Purging" can happen when a cell-turnover active (retinoids, AHA/BHA, some vitamin C) speeds up exfoliation, so microcomedones that were already forming surface faster and sooner. A "reaction" (irritation or clogging) is when a product simply doesn't agree with your skin. The clearest tells are timing, location, and whether it settles.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.0.q: Did this start after introducing a cell-turnover active (a retinoid, AHA/BHA/PHA, or vitamin C)?
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.0.options.0.labe: Yes — I added one of those
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.0.options.1.labe: No — it started with a richer cream, oil, balm or SPF
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.1.q: How long after starting the product did the bumps appear?
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.1.options.2.labe: After 6–8 weeks or longer of steady use
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.2.q: Where are the new bumps showing up?
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.2.options.0.labe: In my usual breakout zones, where I tend to get them anyway
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.2.options.1.labe: In new areas I don't normally break out
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.2.options.2.labe: Everywhere a product touched / where I applied it
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.3.q: What does the skin feel like alongside the bumps?
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.3.options.0.labe: Small surfacing bumps that come and clear faster than usual
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.3.options.1.labe: Stinging, burning, tightness, redness, flaking or itch
KBEAUTY_PURGE.questions.3.options.2.labe: Tiny uniform itchy bumps on forehead/hairline/chest/back
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.headline: This pattern looks like purging — give it time.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.body: Your reaction lines up with purging: it began after a turnover active, within roughly 2–6 weeks, in your usual breakout zones, and clears faster than a normal blemish. Purging is temporary and typically settles within about 4–8 weeks (up to ~12 for stronger retinoids) as your skin adjusts.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.do.0: Keep the active, but pull back the frequency — e.g. 2–3×/week instead of daily — and build up slowly.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.do.1: Buffer it: apply over a light moisturizer, or 'sandwich' between hydrating layers, to ease irritation.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.do.2: Support the barrier with niacinamide, panthenol, ceramides and a gentle hydrator.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.do.3: Wear SPF 50+ every morning — actives make skin more sun-sensitive.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.do.4: Resist the urge to add more actives at once; one change at a time.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.dont.0: Don't quit on day 3 and assume it 'broke you out' — purging needs a few weeks to resolve.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.dont.1: Don't pick or over-exfoliate the surfacing bumps.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.dont.2: Don't stack a second strong active on top while you adjust.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.purge.reassess: If it's still worsening after ~8–12 weeks, treat it as a reaction (below) and re-evaluate the product.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.headline: This pattern looks more like a reaction than purging.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.body: Purging happens where you already break out and only with turnover actives. New bumps in new areas, an immediate response, congestion from a rich cream/oil/SPF, or a flare after 6–8 weeks of steady use all point to the product not agreeing with your skin — not purging.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.do.0: Pause the suspected product and simplify to a gentle cleanser, a basic moisturizer and SPF.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.do.1: Reintroduce one product at a time so you can identify the culprit (patch-test on the jaw first).
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.do.2: If bumps are tiny, uniform and itchy on the forehead/hairline/chest/back, run the Fungal-Acne check below.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.do.3: Look for heavy occlusives, comedogenic oils or fragrance in the product — decode the label below.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.dont.0: Don't push through hoping it'll 'purge out' — non-purging congestion usually doesn't.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.dont.1: Don't add actives onto already-reacting skin.
KBEAUTY_PURGE.outcomes.react.reassess: Persistent, painful or spreading breakouts deserve a professional opinion.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.title: Barrier-Damage Symptom Check
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.subtitle: A surging topic. Tick what you're experiencing — we'll gauge how stressed your barrier looks and map a recovery protocol.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.primer: Your skin barrier is the outer layer of cells and lipids that holds water in and keeps irritants out. Over-exfoliation, too many actives at once, harsh cleansing, or weather can compromise it — leaving skin tight, stingy and reactive. The fix is almost always less, not more.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.0.label: Products that used to feel fine now sting or burn
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.1.label: Persistent tightness, even after moisturizing
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.2.label: New redness, flushing or blotchiness
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.3.label: Flaking, rough patches or peeling
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.4.label: Skin looks tight-shiny or feels 'raw'
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.5.label: Dehydrated yet sometimes oily (over-stripped)
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.6.label: Suddenly reacting to products I tolerated before
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.symptoms.7.label: I've been using strong actives often, or layering several
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.0.headline: Your barrier seems mostly okay — keep it simple.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.0.body: Few of the classic stress signs are present. Maintain a calm, hydration-forward routine and introduce any new active slowly, one at a time.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.1.headline: Several signs point to a stressed barrier — ease off and rebuild.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.1.body: Your skin is showing real signs of strain. The goal for the next 1–2 weeks is to calm, hydrate and rebuild — and to pause anything that exfoliates or sensitizes until comfort returns.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.2.headline: Strong signs of a compromised barrier — strip back to recovery basics.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.levels.2.body: Many stress signs are present. Pare your routine right down to a 3-step recovery core, pause every active, and prioritize comfort. Most barriers rebound within a couple of weeks of consistent, gentle care.
KBEAUTY_BARRIER.rescueBrands.0.note: Birch Juice / Mugwort lines — gentle daily barrier care
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.title: Fungal-Acne (Malassezia) Aware Mode
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.subtitle: A deep-enthusiast rabbit hole. Flip the decoder into Fungal-Acne mode and it flags ingredients commonly reported to feed malassezia yeast.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.primer: "Fungal acne" (the common nickname for malassezia folliculitis) isn't true acne — it's tiny, uniform, often itchy bumps on the forehead, hairline, chest, back and shoulders, driven by a yeast that lives on everyone's skin. That yeast feeds on certain fatty acids and esters, so many enthusiasts avoid those ingredients. This mode is an educational screen, not a diagnosis — see a doctor for itchy, persistent bumps; some cases need antifungal treatment.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.tellTale.0: Tiny, same-size bumps rather than varied pimples
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.tellTale.1: Clustered on forehead, hairline, jaw, chest, back or shoulders
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.tellTale.3: Flares with heat, sweat, occlusion, or after rich oils/creams
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.tellTale.4: Doesn't respond to normal acne products
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.fatty-a: Fatty acids in roughly the C11–C24 range (e.g. lauric, myristic, palmitic, stearic, oleic) are a common food source for malassezia.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.fatty-e: Esters of those fatty acids (often -ate endings like isopropyl myristate, glyceryl stearate, ascorbyl palmitate) are frequently avoided on fungal-safe routines.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.fatty-a: Fatty alcohols (cetyl, stearyl, etc.) are a debated maybe — many tolerate them, but cautious routines limit them.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.plant-o: Most plant oils and butters contain feeding fatty acids; common exceptions reported as lower-risk are squalane, MCT/caprylic-capric triglyceride and mineral oil.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.polysor: Polysorbates and some PEG/sorbitan esters are flagged as possible feeders by cautious routines.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.explainerByFamily.ferment: Some fermented ingredients (e.g. galactomyces) are commonly avoided in strict fungal-safe routines.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.safeNote: Commonly reported as lower-risk on fungal-safe routines.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.safeHelpers: Many people lean on lightweight, ester-light actives such as niacinamide, centella, hyaluronic acid and (as a leave-on for some) sulfur, salicylic acid, zinc pyrithione or ketoconazole — but treatment choices should be guided by a professional.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.decoderEmptyAllSafe: No common malassezia-feeding ingredients flagged in this list. This is an educational screen only, not a guarantee — formulas and individual tolerance vary.
KBEAUTY_FUNGAL.decoderModeHint: Flags esters, fatty acids/alcohols, most oils & butters, polysorbates and certain ferments that are commonly avoided on fungal-safe routines.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.methodology: Position and stage are an editorial read of Korean retailer launches, search interest and social mentions — analysis, not a precise metric. Dated so you can judge how current it is.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.0.label: Glass skin
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.0.blurb: The dewy, poreless “lit-from-within” look that put K-beauty on the global map.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.0.methodology: Mainstream worldwide; search interest plateaued as it became a default beauty goal.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.0.science: A real, achievable hydration-and-glow look from layered moisture + SPF — an aesthetic, not a permanent change to your skin.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.1.label: PDRN “Salmon DNA”
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.1.blurb: Korea’s breakout firming active of 2025-26, racing from clinics into serums, creams and pads.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.1.methodology: Top of Korean retailer launches and search; Western awareness is still early — a classic crossing-out signal.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.1.science: Strong as an injectable; topical-cosmetic evidence is still emerging — expect a hydrated, plumped glow, not injectable-level firming.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.2.label: Exosomes & next-gen
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.2.blurb: Lab-advanced regenerative claims moving from aesthetic clinics into at-home cosmetics.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.2.methodology: High buzz in Korean derma-clinics; cosmetic versions are only just appearing in the West.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.2.science: Exciting science, but rigorous evidence for topical cosmetic exosomes is very limited today — treat as a nice serum, not a clinic substitute.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.3.label: Snail mucin
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.3.blurb: A K-beauty staple that went fully global after viral love for the COSRX essence.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.3.methodology: Now mainstream in the West; steady and no longer a novelty in Korea.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.3.science: A well-liked hydrating, comforting humectant — great for glow and dewiness; “repair” claims are softer than the marketing.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.4.label: Heartleaf (어성초)
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.4.blurb: Houttuynia, the calming hero for oily, troubled skin — powering Anua’s global breakout.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.4.methodology: Peaking in Korea and accelerating in the West via viral toners — actively crossing out.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.4.science: A well-established soothing botanical — the calmer, comfier-skin result is real; the “shrinks pores” framing is the overclaim.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.5.label: Barrier-first skincare
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.5.blurb: Repair the skin barrier first, add actives later — the philosophy behind “less is more”.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.5.methodology: Default advice in both markets; foundational and steady rather than spiking.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.5.science: Well-supported. A healthy barrier (ceramides, gentle care, fewer harsh actives) is the foundation of calm, resilient skin.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.6.label: Microbiome & postbiotics
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.6.blurb: Ferment and postbiotic care to support the skin’s natural balance.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.6.methodology: Rising on both sides; product claims still run ahead of the topical evidence.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.6.science: A genuinely active research field; ferments hydrate and feel great, but “rebalances your microbiome” claims outpace the evidence.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.7.label: Sun stick & reapply
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.7.blurb: Sticks and cushions that make midday SPF reapplication actually happen.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.7.methodology: Huge in Korea; reapplication formats are now crossing into Western routines.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.7.science: Reapplication is the most evidence-backed habit in skincare — just apply enough; thin layers under-deliver the SPF on the label.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.8.label: Skin cycling
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.8.blurb: A West-born, dermatologist-coined 4-night rotation: exfoliate, retinoid, recover, recover.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.8.methodology: Originated in the US and is now filtering INTO Korean routines — a rare crossing-in.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.8.science: A sensible scheduling framework that reduces over-exfoliation and irritation — the method, not a product, is the point.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.9.label: Slugging
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.9.blurb: Sealing the routine with an occlusive overnight — viral on Western SkinTok.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.9.methodology: Peaked in the West and cooling slightly as the “not for acne-prone” nuance spreads.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.9.science: Genuinely helps dry, compromised barriers hold water — but can feel heavy and isn’t ideal for oily or breakout-prone skin.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.10.label: Glazed-donut skin
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.10.blurb: A Western, celebrity-coined reframing of the glass-skin glow.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.10.methodology: Big on Western social platforms; essentially a Western rename of a Korean look.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.10.science: Same idea as glass skin — layered hydration and a dewy finish; an aesthetic, not a skin-health metric.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.11.label: Men’s K-beauty
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.11.blurb: Korea leads the world in men’s skincare — simple, effective and normalized.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.11.methodology: Mature in Korea and growing fast in Western men’s routines — crossing out.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.11.science: Skin doesn’t read gender — the same proven basics (cleanse, hydrate, SPF) work. A real market shift, not a gimmick.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.12.label: Skinimalism / skip-care
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.12.blurb: Curated 4-5 step routines replacing the maximalist 10-step, on both sides of the Pacific.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.12.methodology: Rising globally as a correction to product overload; strong in both markets.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.12.science: Fewer, well-chosen steps reduce irritation and improve consistency — an evidence-aligned correction to overuse.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.13.label: Mugwort (쑥)
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.13.blurb: Artemisia, the traditional hanbang soothing botanical, riding the calming-skincare wave.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.13.methodology: Strong in Korea and building in the West alongside heartleaf and cica — crossing out.
KBEAUTY_RADAR.items.13.science: A comforting, antioxidant-rich botanical — pleasant and soothing; specific “healing” claims outrun the topical evidence.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.0.label: Beef tallow
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.0.claim: A “natural” moisturizer that beats modern creams.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.0.science: Rich and occlusive, so it can soften very dry skin — but there is no evidence it out-performs a formulated moisturizer, and it rates high for clogging pores.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.0.note: Patch-test first; best avoided on oily or breakout-prone skin.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.1.label: Rice water
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.1.claim: A Korean secret for glass skin and brightening.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.1.science: A pleasant, mild humectant-and-antioxidant rinse that adds gentle hydration and glow; any “brightening” is subtle and not a substitute for proven actives.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.1.note: Harmless for most — keep expectations modest.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.2.label: Skin flooding
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.2.claim: Layer humectants on damp skin to “flood” it with moisture.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.2.science: Sound technique — humectants grab water best on damp skin, then a cream seals it in. Basically good layering with a catchy name.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.3.label: Morning shed
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.3.claim: Pile on overnight layers, then peel off a “transformed” face at dawn.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.3.science: Mostly theatrical — overnight masks and patches do hydrate, but the dramatic reveal is a look, not a lasting skin upgrade.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.3.note: Heavy layering can clog or irritate some skin.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.4.label: DIY lemon / vinegar acids
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.4.claim: Natural acids for brightening and clearing breakouts.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.4.science: Risky and unreliable — DIY citrus and vinegar have an uncontrolled pH and can burn or disrupt the barrier. A formulated AHA/BHA is safer and more effective.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.4.note: Can cause chemical burns and sun sensitivity — skip this one.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.5.label: Ice facials / skin icing
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.5.claim: De-puff and permanently shrink your pores.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.5.science: Temporarily de-puffs and feels refreshing; any pore “shrinking” is brief. Fine in moderation.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.5.note: Don’t hold ice on bare skin too long — wrap it to avoid a cold burn.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.6.label: Retinol sandwich
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.6.science: A legitimate buffering method that genuinely improves retinoid tolerance for sensitive or new users.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.7.label: Sunscreen “contouring”
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.7.claim: Skip SPF on some areas to “contour” with a tan.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.7.science: A genuinely harmful trend — uneven sunscreen means uneven UV damage and pigmentation, the opposite of healthy skin.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.7.note: Always apply SPF evenly to the whole face.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.8.label: Glazed-donut skin
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.8.science: Layered hydration plus a dewy finish — a real, achievable look (the same idea as glass skin).
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.9.label: “Pore-filter” primers
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.9.claim: Blur pores into invisibility like a filter.
KBEAUTY_VIRALCHECK.items.9.science: Silicone-style blurring primers really do soften the look of pores for the day — a cosmetic, temporary optical effect, not a change to the pores themselves.

KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.0.title: How we read trends
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.0.body: We position each trend on a Korea-vs-West attention map from three inputs: Korean retailer launches and best-seller movement, search interest, and social mentions. Lifecycle stage and crossover direction are an editorial read of those signals — analysis, not a precise metric — and every card is dated so you can judge how current it is.
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.1.title: How we grade the evidence
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.1.body: Each trend and viral claim gets one of four honest verdicts: ✅ Science-backed (well-supported), 🔬 Promising (real but emerging evidence), ⚖️ Works, but… (context-dependent or partly oversold), 💨 More hype than proof. Verdicts use cosmetic structure-function language (helps / supports / improves the appearance of) and never make medical claims.
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.2.title: Sources we rely on
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.2.body: We cross-check against public, authoritative references — peer-reviewed research (PubMed), the American Academy of Dermatology, the EU CosIng ingredient database, and Korea’s MFDS — plus named, dated Korean retail and review signals (Olive Young, Hwahae, Naver). Links go out to the primary source so you can verify for yourself.
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.3.title: How we stay current
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.3.body: The radar and viral watchlist are reviewed about monthly; the evidence ledger and bestseller board about quarterly. Each section shows its own “reviewed” date, and a section quietly flags itself as “under review” when it is overdue — so the page tells you the truth about its own freshness.
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.4.title: Claims & safety policy
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.4.body: This is general educational information, not personalized medical advice. We use structure-function wording, keep honest hedges, and flag anything risky. For a persistent or serious skin concern, see a dermatologist.
KBEAUTY_TRUST.items.5.title: Affiliate disclosure

KBEAUTY_REPORT.intro: Our quarterly read on where K-beauty is heading: the trends gaining real momentum, the viral claims worth your time (and the ones worth skipping), and the honest evidence behind the headlines — compiled from the radar, the evidence ledger and this quarter’s reality checks.
trend.pdrn.science: Strong as an injectable; topical-cosmetic evidence is still emerging. Expect a hydrated, plumped glow — not injectable-level firming.
trend.barrier.science: Well-supported. A healthy barrier (ceramides, gentle care, fewer harsh actives) is the foundation of calm, resilient skin.
trend.microbiome.science: A genuinely active research field; ferments hydrate and feel great, but specific “rebalances your microbiome” product claims still outpace the topical evidence.
trend.exosome.science: Exciting science, but rigorous evidence for topical cosmetic exosomes is very limited today. Treat as a nice serum, not a clinic substitute.
trend.heartleaf.science: A well-established soothing botanical — the “calmer, comfier skin” result is real; the “shrinks pores” framing is the overclaim.
trend.mens.science: Skin doesn’t read gender — the same proven basics (cleanse, hydrate, SPF) work. A real, sensible market shift, not a gimmick.
trend.suncare.science: Reapplication is the most evidence-backed habit in skincare. Sticks/cushions help compliance — just apply enough; thin layers under-deliver SPF.
trend.skinimalism.science: Fewer, well-chosen steps reduce irritation and improve consistency — a solid, evidence-aligned correction to product overload.
